proposal.description: Start from A; Shorten the 1.11s pause at the end of 'His name was Smoot. Nearly 70 years later, that br...'. (aimed at A's finding at 12.9-14.0s: The final silent, static hold does not add a new payoff or a clearly intentional closing beat.)
proposal.expected_improvement: A cleaner, more decisive finish after the real-photo proof, reducing the chance of attention dropping during the silent static hold.

protected_strengths.item: The unusual opening premise and clear illustration of measuring a bridge with a person's body.
The explicit step-by-step explanation: laying him down, marking his height, and moving him repeatedly.
The Smoot name reveal and real bridge photo that establish the unit and show that the markings remain.

tradeoffs: Viewers get 1.11 seconds less time to inspect the final bridge image and painted marking.
proposal.why_smallest: It removes only the exact low-severity weakness identified in A while leaving all narration, claims, captions, explanatory steps, and payoff imagery intact. Swapping in B material would sacrifice A's consistently preferred comprehension and progression, while zooming risks cropping captions.
proposal.selector_reason: A was preferred overall for first-time comprehension, information progression, and visual-narration alignment. Both independent audits found its only supported weakness to be the unproductive final hold, so trimming that pause is the narrowest evidence-backed improvement.
